subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: Should OpenClaw's durable memory lifecycle MVP live in the default memory-core plugin as typed record flows, in memory-wiki as a provenance-rich knowledge layer, or behind a new/expanded memory plugin API first?
rationale: The current implementation has search/get, promotion, Dreaming review artifacts, and memory-wiki supplements, but the requested lifecycle semantics would define durable storage and operator behavior across plugin and core boundaries.

options.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
options.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow CLI/tool/UI flows for review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict resolution.

options.title: Route to memory-wiki knowledge workflows
options.body: Treat this as a wiki curation problem and extend memory-wiki's claim/provenance/apply flows rather than changing the default memory record model now.

options.title: Add plugin API seams before implementation
options.body: Define a memory lifecycle SDK contract so bundled and external memory plugins can implement the flows consistently.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
recommendation.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow CLI/tool/UI flows for review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: The central memory implementation history in this checkout points most clearly to Vincent Koc's recent cross-file memory-core work.
